section_summary: This section documents U.S. and Allied diplomatic reporting and internal analyses on the fall of the Abe Cabinet and the formation of Admiral Mitsumasa Yonai's Cabinet in Japan in mid-January 1940. Dispatches and telegrams from Tokyo, Paris, Chungking, and Shanghai assess the intense political struggle between the Japanese Army and the Emperor's palace advisers, international reactions, and Japanese policy declarations regarding the China Incident, the United States, and the Soviet Union. The section also includes War Department correspondence regarding the unauthorized circulation of Captain Bonner F. Fellers' 1934–1935 Command and General Staff School monograph, 'The Psychology of the Japanese Soldier,' alongside the text of the study itself.

subfiles.about: Adviser Hornbeck analyzes Tokyo telegram No. 20 regarding the formation of the Yonai Cabinet and the political contest between the Japanese Army and the Emperor's advisers.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck doubts the Yonai Cabinet will last, disagreeing with Grew's optimism on China moderation though expecting Yonai to resist close Axis/Soviet alignment amid Army-advisor maneuvering.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by the Adviser on Political Relations (Hornbeck) on Cabinet Changes in Japan

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports on the selection of Admiral Mitsumasa Yonai as Prime Minister and the contest between the Army and palace advisers over cabinet formation.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, United States Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits a three-section confidential telegram analyzing the sudden appointment of Admiral Mitsumasa Yonai as Prime Minister following the resignation of the Abe Cabinet. Grew details the secret contest between Lord Privy Seal Yuasa and the Army leadership, noting the Army's reluctance to assume direct responsibility for mounting economic problems and the active intervention of the Emperor. While ultra-nationalist organs criticized the appointment as engineered by court advisers, Grew views Yonai's moderate temperament as the most satisfactory development possible for U.S.-Japanese relations and looks for progressive moderation in Japan's China policy.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 20 (Sections 1–3) on Formation of the Yonai Cabinet

subfiles.about: Ambassador Bullitt reports French diplomatic information regarding the Yonai Cabinet, Soviet aid to China, and possible Japanese designs on Soviet Siberia.
subfiles.from: William C. Bullitt, United States Ambassador to France
subfiles.summary: Bullitt reports Chauvel calling Yonai a Western-friendly moderate skeptical of Soviet talks and Wang's regime, while Léger suggested Japan might exploit Soviet weakness to attack Siberia.
subfiles.title: Paris Telegram No. 79 (Sections 1–2) on French Views of the Japanese Cabinet and Far Eastern Situation

subfiles.about: Consul General Peck transmits a summary of Chungking press editorial reaction to the fall of the Abe Cabinet and the selection of Admiral Yonai.
subfiles.from: Willys R. Peck, Counselor of Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.summary: Peck summarizes Chungking press calling Abe's fall military-engineered and Yonai merely transitional, convinced Japanese China aggression will continue despite U.S./Soviet outreach.
subfiles.title: Chungking Telegram No. 30 on Chinese Press Reaction to the Fall of the Abe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports the complete ministerial roster of the newly formed Yonai Cabinet and summarizes Japanese press assessments.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, United States Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Yonai's 28-hour Cabinet formation (Arita, Hata, Yoshida, Sakurauchi, Kodama, Ishiwata); press criticized its lack of cohesion, expecting Arita to adjust Western ties while keeping Axis friendship.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 23 Announcing the Yonai Cabinet Lineup and Press Reactions

subfiles.about: A Department of State Division of Far Eastern Affairs paraphrase and summary of Tokyo Telegram No. 23 on the Yonai Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase details Yonai's full Cabinet lineup and biographies, press criticism of disunity, and expected diplomatic outreach to the U.S., Britain, Russia, and the Axis.
subfiles.title: Department of State Paraphrase of Tokyo Telegram No. 23 Regarding the Yonai Cabinet

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports statements made to the press by Prime Minister Yonai and Foreign Minister Arita regarding foreign policy and treaty relations.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, United States Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Grew summarizes Yonai's and Arita's first interviews: continuing China policy, independent foreign policy seeking U.S./British/Soviet readjustment, Yangtze reopening, and a firm Anti-Comintern Pact.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 26 Reporting Press Interviews of Prime Minister Yonai and Foreign Minister Arita

subfiles.about: Consul General Gauss summarizes Shanghai press editorial reactions to the formation and prospects of the new Yonai Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Clarence E. Gauss, United States Consul General, Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Gauss relays Shanghai press calling Yonai a moderate best choice but doubting civilian control over the military; Wang's paper hopes for Konoe-declaration support, others see it as transitional.
subfiles.title: Shanghai Telegram No. 46 on Shanghai Press Reaction to the Yonai Cabinet

subfiles.about: Alfred Bergman sends Secretary of State Cordell Hull an enclosed study on the Japanese situation written by his classmate Bonner F. Fellers.
subfiles.summary: Bergman sends Hull a classmate's study on Japan, praising it as brilliant and fundamental for Far Eastern understanding.
subfiles.title: Letter from Alfred Bergman to Secretary of State Cordell Hull Enclosing Study on Japan

subfiles.about: Colonel McCabe directs that Captain Bonner F. Fellers be reprimanded and ordered to recall all copies of his improperly circulated C&GSS research study.
subfiles.from: Colonel E. R. W. McCabe, Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, War Department
subfiles.summary: McCabe reports Fellers' research study used classified attaché/G-2 material; the Secretary of War ordered his reprimand and recall of circulated copies amid delicate relations.
subfiles.title: War Department Memorandum for The Adjutant General regarding Improper Disposition of Research Study by Capt. Bonner F. Fellers

subfiles.about: Captain Bonner F. Fellers presents an extensive analytical study on the psychological, cultural, and spiritual factors driving the Japanese soldier and Imperial Army.
subfiles.from: Captain Bonner F. Fellers, Coast Artillery Corps, U.S. Army
keywords: The Psychology of the Japanese Soldier
subfiles.summary: Captain Bonner F. Fellers' Command and General Staff School individual research study examines the psychological, religious, and historical foundations of the Japanese soldier, demonstrating that military psychology is inseparable from national Shinto belief and absolute devotion to the Emperor. The study traces Japanese history, the warrior code of the Samurai, the institutionalization of hara-kiri and refusal to surrender, the Meiji Restoration, and the rise of modern military nationalism and Pan-Asiatic ambitions led by General Sadao Araki. Fellers assesses Japanese army training, morale, and combat methods, noting severe deficiencies in mechanization, artillery doctrine, staff planning, and strategic flexibility despite supreme infantry offensive spirit. (Note: in this bound volume, concluding pages 97–99 and bibliography pages 100–104 precede the title page, commendations by C&GSS and Manuel L. Quezon, and Chapters I–IV on pages 105–137).
subfiles.title: Individual Research Study: 'The Psychology of the Japanese Soldier'
